statement: An independent three-edge star with distinct terminals a,b,c cannot have boundary-connectivity law assigning probability 1/2 to a|b|c and 1/2 to abc and zero to each pair-only partition.
assumptions: Three star edges open independently with probabilities p_a,p_b,p_c in [0,1].
proof: If P(abc)=p_a p_b p_c=1/2 then all p_i>0. Pair-only probabilities are p_a p_b(1-p_c), p_a p_c(1-p_b), p_b p_c(1-p_a). Their vanishing forces all p_i=1, contradicting product 1/2.
remaining_gap: Does not rule out approximate macroscopic comparison or correlated gadgets; does not establish the target.

statement: For a finite undirected graph with k>=3 distinct terminals and independent Bernoulli edges, positive probabilities of both extreme terminal partitions force positive probability of an intermediate partition. If m optional-edge probabilities lie in [epsilon,1-epsilon], 0<epsilon<=1/2, its partition law is at total variation distance at least min(q,1-q,epsilon^m) from the all-or-none selector of parameter 0<q<1.
assumptions: Finite graph, open-path connectivity, k>=3 distinct terminals.
Edges mutually independent with probabilities in [0,1].
Quantitative clause requires the stated optional-edge bound.
proof: Delete forced-closed edges and contract forced-open components. A terminal-spanning minimal tree of optional edges exists if all-connected has positive probability. Delete one edge from that tree and close all other optional edges. Each side contains a terminal, yielding exactly two terminal blocks with positive probability, at least epsilon^m. If an extreme has zero probability use its selector mass for the TV bound instead.
remaining_gap: No uniform bound for growing gadgets and no continuum transfer.

statement: For finite independent-coordinate product laws mu and nu and a [0,1]-valued function F, their expectation difference is the sum of signed one-coordinate replacement expectations in hybrid exterior laws H_i. Its absolute value is bounded by sum_i TV(mu_i,nu_i) E_H_i osc_i(F), where H_i uses nu before coordinate i and mu after it.
assumptions: Both endpoint laws and every hybrid law are products.
F depends on the same named coordinate state spaces and has values in [0,1].
proof: Telescope adjacent product laws; condition on their common exterior. Local independence gives the signed finite sum. Subtract the local minimum of F and bound the zero-mass signed measure by TV times oscillation. Average and sum. No independence between sensitivity events is assumed.
remaining_gap: No actual square-to-triangular comparison or bound on its signed defect is supplied.

statement: A fair all-or-none three-terminal selector and an independent three-arm star with arm probability 1/sqrt(2) have every pair connection probability equal to 1/2. After the same deterministic exterior wiring a~c, their connection-to-b crossing probabilities differ by (2-sqrt(2))/4.
assumptions: Star arms are mutually independent Bernoulli(1/sqrt(2)).
Exterior a~c wiring is deterministic and crossing means b connected to either a or c.
proof: Star pair connection probability is s^2, triple probability s^3. Inclusion-exclusion gives the wired crossing 2s^2-s^3=1-1/(2sqrt(2)), compared with selector crossing 1/2.
counterexample: All three pair-marginal checks pass, while the same exterior crossing check fails by about 0.1464466094.
remaining_gap: A finite replacement counterexample does not refute conformal invariance or approximate universality.

statement: A genuine mesh-dependent comparison between square-bond p=1/2 and triangular-site p=1/2 percolation has total signed macroscopic crossing defect tending to zero, with the necessary boundary and exploration controls.
assumptions: Actual endpoint models, specified domain approximation and boundary arcs.
A valid common-coordinate or conditional-kernel comparison must be constructed.
remaining_gap: This entire comparison estimate is unproved; interface identification also remains.
